kind.title: Where does it run?
kind.builtinDescription: Runs on this deployment's own Bot. Nothing to host or connect — it is ready the moment it is created.
kind.managedDescription: Runs on an agent you host, spoken to over AG-UI. This server dials your endpoint on every run.
kind.unavailable: Not available here: this deployment has no Bot of its own for a coworker to run on.

kind.keyNote: Sent as an Authorization header on every run, and kept in the credential vault.

handoff.title: Bots it may ask
handoff.intro: Who this Bot may ask, not who may ask it. What the asked Bot says comes back into the conversation that asked, relayed and attributed.
handoff.switchedOffDescription: These grants are kept but none takes effect until handing work between Bots is switched back on.
handoff.cannotGrant: This coworker cannot hand work on.
handoff.cannotGrantDescription: This deployment has nowhere to record which Bots it may hand work to, so there is nothing to grant it. It can still be asked by Bots that can.
handoff.noOthersDescription: When this deployment has more Bots, this is where this one is allowed to ask them.
handoff.adminDecides: An administrator decides which Bots may be asked.

proposed.clash: There is already a {{title}} here, which is {{ownership}}. Names do not have to be unique, but two with the same name are hard to tell apart in a channel list.
proposed.noCreateYet: Nothing is created until you press the button.
proposed.name: Name
proposed.standingInstructions: Its standing instructions. This text is given to a model on every turn.
proposed.arrivesPrivate: It arrives private, with no address, no connector and no tool. Anything it needs to reach is granted on its profile afterwards.
proposed.unwritable: The coworker could not be created as written, so nothing was asked of you. It is being redrafted.

proactive.none: No suggestions right now. Bots with background research on will suggest next steps here.
proactive.title: Background research
proactive.intro: On by default once you start a conversation with just this Bot: it looks through the apps it can already read every four hours, forms memories for you to review and suggests next steps. It can only read: it cannot send messages, change anything in an app, or use a browser or computer. Turn it off or remove it and it stays that way.
proactive.focusPlaceholder: Open issues assigned to me and questions waiting on me
proactive.dialogDescription: It reads on a schedule and delivers what it suggests to a channel it is in.

cleanup.title: Cleanup
cleanup.description: What OpenBot still holds of what you forgot, and whether controlled copies are cleared.
cleanup.claim: All controlled copies are cleared. Deleted data is verified gone, finished task payloads are past their retention window, and controlled backups are purged.
cleanup.external: Logs kept by model providers outside OpenBot aren't controlled copies. Their retention is checked separately.
cleanup.onHoldNote: A restored backup is being replayed. Checks resume after it lands.
cleanup.payloadsPending: {{n}} are past the retention window and still held.
cleanup.payloadsUnchecked: This OpenBot couldn't check right now.
cleanup.payloadsNoWindow: No retention window is set, so there's nothing to measure against.
cleanup.backupsCleared: Every copy taken before your deletions is purged.
cleanup.backupsPending: {{n}} copies taken before your deletions aren't purged yet.
cleanup.backupsNone: No backup is registered yet, so there's no evidence they're cleared.

github.title: GitHub event sources
github.description: Register a repository, then add its webhook in GitHub using the endpoint below and the same secret. Subscribe a responsibility to an event such as issues.opened.

kindHelp.webhook: POST JSON to the URL with the authorization header (or Standard Webhooks signature headers). 200 means accepted and queued, not finished.
kindHelp.github: In the repository's Settings → Webhooks, set the payload URL to this URL, content type application/json, and the secret to the key.
kindHelp.linear: In Linear, Settings → API → Webhooks: set the URL, then paste the signing secret Linear shows here.
kindHelp.sentry: In a Sentry internal integration, set the webhook URL, then paste the integration's client secret here.
kindHelp.pagerduty: In PagerDuty, Integrations → Generic Webhooks (v3): set the URL, then paste the secret shown on creation here.
kindHelp.email: Send or forward mail to this address to start a run.
kindHelp.slack: Fires from Slack events delivered through this Bot's Slack pairing. Messages from before the trigger existed are ignored.
